leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist - November 2023
leads.documents: Federal criminalization of LGBT activism applicable in Khakassia; leading, participating in, funding, or displaying symbols like rainbow flag punishable by prison
leads.detail: Cited in text as November 2023 ruling following Ministry of Justice lawsuit citing 'various signs of an extremist orientation'; closed-door hearing with no defendants; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Federal law banning gender transition - July 2023
leads.documents: Nationwide including Khakassia ban on gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition; core trans-visitor safety status
leads.detail: Cited as 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright'; no URL visible

leads.title: Expanded 'propaganda' law - 2022
leads.documents: Nationwide ban applicable in Khakassia on distribution of materials promoting 'non-traditional' relationships to any age and materials making minors interested in gender transition
leads.detail: Cited as 2013 law criminalising distribution among minors, expanded in 2022 to anyone regardless of age group plus gender transition interest; no URL visible

leads.title: Ministry of Justice Unified List of Terrorist and Extremist Organizations - entry 22 March 2024
leads.documents: Official enforcement list entry for 'international LGBT social movement and its structural units' used by police/courts including in Khakassia
leads.detail: Cited as formally added 22 March 2024 as 'Mezhdunarodnoe obshchestvennoe dvizhenie LGBT i ego strukturnye podrazdeleniya'; no URL visible

leads.title: Fedotova and Others v. Russia - European Court of Human Rights, 2021
leads.documents: ECHR ruling that failure to offer any legal recognition to same-sex relationships violates human rights; documents lack of unions/marriage in Russia including Khakassia
leads.detail: Cited as 2021 ECHR Strasbourg case; notes Russia left court in 2022; no URL visible

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights ruling on pride parade bans - 2010
leads.documents: Finding that Russian cities discriminated by refusing pride permits; documents enforcement machinery for assembly bans applicable to Khakassia
leads.detail: Cited as 2010 fine following systemic refusals, case alleged by Nikolay Alexeyev, Moscow City Court upheld yearly ban through 2012; no URL visible

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert advisors report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Panel of five experts condemning wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya; institutional documentation of anti-LGBTQ enforcement pattern in Russia
leads.detail: Cited as report issued 13 April 2017; no URL visible

leads.title: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Confirmation that persecution of LGBTQ persons took place and was ignored by authorities
leads.detail: Cited as December 2018 OSCE report confirming claims; no URL visible

leads.title: ILGA-Europe ranking - 2024
leads.documents: Institutional comparative rights status: Russia ranked worst of 49 European countries surveyed, followed by Turkey and Azerbaijan; context for Khakassia risk
leads.detail: Cited as 2024 status ranked worst out of 49; also 2016 second least friendly and May 2019 46th of 49; no URL visible

leads.title: Amnesty International assessment of extremist ruling
leads.documents: Human-rights institutional characterization of Supreme Court ruling as 'shameful and absurd' and effectively criminalizing LGBTQ advocacy
leads.detail: Cited as Amnesty International description; no URL visible
